title: Ivo and the Archive
premise: Xenolinguist Wren Delacroix has spent seven years alone on Relay Station Kestrel, tending a beacon whose original orders were erased from every record. When the ship Perihelion returns from deep space carrying a crew aged backward into childhood, the beacon's true purpose surfaces: it is a countdown, and Wren has been its unwitting keeper. The message it holds can end the war between Earth and the Vessic Concord by proving both species descend from the same vanished civilization — but delivering it means exposing the Admiralty's decades-long cover-up. Wren must choose between the institution that gave her a place to belong and the truth that could save millions, and in the end she broadcasts the message, accepting exile as the war ends and the 'children' of the Perihelion, remembering their future, become the first citizens of a shared history.
about_author: Mirabel Hartwell is the pen name of a former radio astronomer who spent a decade listening to signals no one else believed mattered. They write quiet, character-driven science fiction about the people who keep the lights on at the edge of things.

chapters.title: The Keeper of Small Hours
chapters.summary: POV Wren. On isolated Relay Station Kestrel, Wren maintains the beacon and records her dreams, which have shifted into an untranslatable alien cadence. A routine supply drop brings news of the war's worsening stalemate and a curt order to decommission. Her quiet devotion to a station nobody remembers commissioning establishes her loneliness and loyalty — and ends when the beacon suddenly answers her dreams.

chapters.title: Perihelion
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The ship Perihelion docks, its crew aged backward into children who nonetheless speak with adult authority — and one of them, Commander Ashe, recognizes the beacon's signal. Through the child-crew's fragmentary testimony, Wren learns the beacon is a countdown keyed to her linguistic work. An Admiralty salvage team arrives with orders to seize the station, and Wren must hide the truth from both sides, torn between obedience and the children who trust her.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Remembers
chapters.summary: POV alternating Wren and child-Commander Ashe. Decoding the beacon in the station's depths, they uncover the Admiralty's cover-up: the war began over a discovery both sides were told was a weapon. The salvage team turns hostile, and Wren transmits a false all-clear to buy time, committing her first act of open betrayal of her institution. Ashe's adult memories surface fully, revealing the message's final key — and that broadcasting it will brand Wren a traitor forever.

chapters.title: A Message in Every Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Wren. With the station breached and countdown at zero, Wren broadcasts the beacon's message in the alien cadence she has dreamed for seven years — the proof that Earth and the Vessic share one origin. Weapons stand down mid-strike as the signal propagates. In the aftermath, Wren accepts exile and decommissioning, but the child-crew chooses to stay with her, and together they begin translating a shared future. Belonging, she realizes, was never the institution's to give.
